title: Point your repo at the website
concept: git remote add origin, git remote -v

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Your laptop does not know that website page exists yet.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: A **remote** is a nickname for a copy of the project somewhere else.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Almost everyone names the main remote `origin`. It is just a habit, not a rule.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Add it, then run `git remote -v` to check it. The `-v` means verbose, so it prints the full address.

items.text: Add a remote called origin pointing at the festival site

hints: You need to tell git the web address of the copy online, and give it a nickname.
`git remote add <nickname> <address>` saves it. The address is https://github.com/lantern-labs/festival-site.git
Run `git remote add origin https://github.com/lantern-labs/festival-site.git`, then `git remote -v`.
recap: `git remote add origin <address>` saves a nickname for the copy online. `git remote -v` lists your remotes.

cheatSheet.summary: Save the address of the copy online under the name origin
List the remotes and their addresses
